newsitem.title: CANADA: TimberWest says it is up for sale.
newsitem.headline: TimberWest says it is up for sale.

text.p: TimberWest Forest Ltd and its 52-percent owner Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd said Friday they agreed to seek potential buyers of TimberWest.
Fletcher Canada is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd. TimberWest, a lumber and logging company, was spun off by Fletcher Canada, a pulp and paper company, in 1993.
With 30.6 million shares outstanding, TimberWest has a market capitalization of about C$520 million. Its stock gained C$0.90 to C$17 before being halted on the Toronto exchange.
In a joint statement, the companies said they would consider "all alternatives" and that a sale was being sought "with a view to maximizing value for all TimberWest shareholders."

TimberWest chief financial officer Wanda Costouros said Fletcher's move to sell its stake essentially meant the whole company was up for sale. An offer for its 52 percent would in all likelihood have to be extended to the company's minority shareholders, she said. A Fletcher spokesman said it was selling its stake to "sharpen our focus on the paper business which is our core business."
This would also enable TimberWest to "find an owner totally committed" to its business, he said.
Any transaction would probably be subject to approval of British Columbia's forest ministry.

TimberWest said it is one of Canada's biggest public companies focusing on lumber. It has five lumbermills in British Columbia with combined annual capacity of 685 million board feet of lumber and 1.5 million cubic meters of wood chips. It holds Crown timber tenures and owns 210,000 hectares of private timberlands with annual harvest of 4.2 million cubic meters.
Fletrcher has capacity to produce 2.2 million tonnes of newsprint, groundwood specialty papers, coated paper, market pulp and containerboard at four mills in Canada and the United States.
Analysts said the strategy of putting the entire company up for sale to a single buyer, rather than a public offering of Fletcher's stake, was aimed at winning the highest price.
"You would get a better price. These (wood products) stocks are not so hot these days. It's not a great public market," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

Among the forest companies that might be interested are West Fraser Timber Co Ltd, Canfor Corp, Slocan Forest Products Ltd and Donohue Inc, analysts said. Canfor declined comment. Officials at the other firms were not immediately available for comment.
Jake Kerr, president of privately held Lignum Ltd said his company "will have a look" at TimberWest.
"TimberWest will be of interest to a number of people...It is a well run, well regarded company," he said.
Forest companies have been scrambling to find new sources of wood fiber in British Columbia.
The British Columbia government's moves to create new parks and reduce timber harvests have reduced supply. Meanwhile, new government regulations and fees have increased costs.
Those policies and a lack of enthusiasm for solid wood products at parent Fletcher Challenge Ltd are probably behind Fletcher Canada's move, one analyst speculated.
But he said TimberWest will likely find many suitors.
"There will be a whole slew of companies interested. There could be a number of bidders," he said.
-- Cynthia Osterman
-- Reuters Vancouver Bureau (604) 664-7314
